```{r Hannah's Hypotheses}

### H1: Categorical IV - Continuous/Composite DV

# Country of residence (categorical IV) - Individualistic values (composite)

# One's social ideologies are indicative of their country of residence, suggesting that one's country of residence may be a predictor of one's individualistic values.

### H2: Continuous - Continuous 

Relationship length (continuous) - Intensity of love feelings (continuous) 

Love may fluctuate throughout a relationship, given that earlier love may feel stronger and more passionate, whereas later love leads to a prioritization of commitment and longevity. Given this, intensity of love feelings may spike earlier in a relationship and reach a plateau in later years.

```


```{r loading data and packages}

raw <-read.csv("data/raw/data_doctored.csv")

library("reshape2")
library("ggplot2")
library("ggrain")
```

```{r configuring useful data set}

###

data <- raw[ ,c("ResponseId", "Sex_birth", "Relationship_status", 
                "Country_raised", "Individualism_col_1", 
                "Individualism_col_2", "Individualism_col_4", 
                "Relationship_length", "Love_how_much_1")]


```

```{r checking NA's}

#count na
sum(is.na(data$ResponseId))

#count blank
sum(data$ResponseId=="",na.rm=TRUE)

#count duplicates
sum(duplicated(data$ResponseId))

#inspect records with missing or blank IDs
missingId <- which(is.na(data$ResponseId))
data[missingId,]

#remove the known empty record with no ID, then check the row count
data <- data[!is.na(data$ResponseId),]

#! indicates the opposite, "no"

```

```{r missing values}

data[, 5:7] <- apply(data[ , 5:7], 2, function(x) {
  ifelse(x <1 | x > 7, NA, x)
})

```

```{r recoding sex}
#codebook: 0 = Male, 1 = Female, 2 = Intersex
table(data$Sex_birth,useNA="ifany")

#turn sex_birth into a factor with labels Male, Female, and Intersex
data$Sex_birth <- factor(data$Sex_birth,
                         levels = c(0,1,2),
                         labels = c("Male","Female","Intersex"))

table(data$Sex_birth,useNA="ifany")

```

```{r individualism}
## checking if numeric
is.numeric(data[,5])
is.numeric(data[,6])
is.numeric(data[,7])

# making these columns numeric
data[,5:7] <- lapply(data[,5:7], as.numeric)

# creating a total account of individualist questions
data$individualistTotal <- rowSums(data[,5:7],na.rm=FALSE)

# create reversed mean of individualist to measure individualism
data$individualism <- 8 - (rowMeans(data[ , 5:7], na.rm = TRUE))
## NOW: higher === greater individualism; lower == greater collectivism


```



```{r P1 plotting}

### P1: Country where one is raised, between Germany and USA, influences
### an individual's level of individualism

###JK: Standardize country names before selecting your two groups, and match the hypothesis to Country_raised. ###
# Country_raised records where respondents spent most of childhood. Update the initial hypothesis, which currently says country of residence.
# The data contain USA, "USA " with a trailing space, and United States. Your current filter excludes the latter two versions, which each occur 50 times.
# data$Country_raised <- trimws(data$Country_raised)
# data$Country_raised[data$Country_raised == "United States"] <- "USA"
# GermanyUSAData <- data[data$Country_raised %in% c("Germany", "USA") & !is.na(data$individualism), ]
# table(GermanyUSAData$Country_raised, useNA = "ifany")
# Also correct "Gernany" to "Germany" in the axis labels below.
###  End of comment ###

# data set that just includes people raised in Germany or the USA
GermanyUSAData <- data[data$Country_raised %in% c("Germany", "USA"), ]


H1Rain <- ggplot(data = GermanyUSAData,
aes(x = Country_raised,
y = individualism,
fill = Country_raised)) +
labs(x = "Raised in Germany versus USA",
y = "Level of Individualism",
fill = "Germany vs USA") +
scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Gernany", "USA")) +
scale_fill_discrete(labels = c("Germany", "USA")) +
geom_rain(alpha=.5) 

H1Rain

```
